title: Irritable Bowel Syndrome: Primary Care Diagnosis and Red-Flag Exclusion

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult primary-care positive diagnosis of IBS, limited exclusion tests and red-flag referral.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national irritable bowel syndrome guideline was identified in the sources opened on 14 October 2026. NICE guidance is an international comparator pending Saudi/local adaptation.
SFDA product registration was not verified; any medicine selection requires the current Saudi Drug Information register and hospital formulary.
Local colorectal and ovarian-cancer referral pathways require confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Disordered gut-brain signalling alters motility and visceral sensation. Symptoms fluctuate with meals, stress and bowel habit. There is no single confirmatory biomarker. A positive symptom-based diagnosis avoids unnecessary repeated testing after red flags are excluded.
keyMechanisms: Disordered gut-brain signalling alters motility and visceral sensation.
Symptoms fluctuate with meals, stress and bowel habit.
There is no single confirmatory biomarker.
A positive symptom-based diagnosis avoids unnecessary repeated testing after red flags are excluded.

symptoms: Abdominal pain or discomfort, bloating and altered stool frequency or form.
physicalSigns: Abdominal examination is often normal; document tenderness, mass, weight and hydration.
redFlags: Unintentional weight loss, rectal bleeding, abdominal/rectal mass, anaemia or inflammatory features require the relevant urgent pathway.
precipitants: Meals, stress, gastroenteritis and particular foods may precede symptoms.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Positive coeliac serology while eating gluten.
Bleeding, weight loss, nocturnal symptoms or objective inflammation.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Meets the NICE symptom cluster without alarm features
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Make a positive diagnosis after limited exclusion testing.
ruleIn.normalValue: No persistent pain or bowel-habit disturbance

clinicalManagement.title: Check alarm features
actions: Record weight trend, bleeding, anaemia symptoms, masses, family history and inflammatory features.
Refer through the relevant urgent pathway when an alarm feature is present.

clinicalManagement.title: Make a positive diagnosis
clinicalManagement.timeframe: After initial assessment and limited tests
actions: Apply the NICE symptom cluster and obtain FBC, CRP/ESR and coeliac serology.
Do not order colonoscopy or imaging solely to confirm typical IBS without alarm features.

clinicalManagement.title: Explain and link to management
actions: Explain the gut-brain disorder and the reason further routine exclusion tests are not required.
Agree symptom goals, safety-net triggers and review; use the linked management-ladder topic.

medicationPlan.note: Diagnosis and red-flag exclusion do not require a medicine.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Abdominal pain/discomfort relieved by defaecation or associated with altered stool frequency/form, plus at least 2 supporting features in NICE CG61.

teaching.scope: Adult primary-care positive diagnosis of IBS, limited exclusion tests and red-flag referral.
learningObjectives: Diagnose IBS positively after limited testing.
pitfalls: Diagnosing IBS in the presence of alarm features.
Repeating broad investigations without a new clinical reason.
keyPoints: Coeliac serology is part of initial testing.
Routine colonoscopy is not required for a typical presentation without red flags.

references.title: NICE CG61: Irritable bowel syndrome in adults: diagnosis and management

patientEducation: Explain expected fluctuation, alarm symptoms and when to return.
lifestyleAndDiet: Keep a symptom-food-bowel diary while maintaining a balanced diet.
mdtReferrals: Primary care; gastroenterology or dietetics when diagnosis or control remains uncertain.
dischargeCriteria: Positive diagnosis recorded, initial tests reviewed, no alarm feature and follow-up route agreed.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review response and reconsider the diagnosis if bleeding, weight loss, anaemia, nocturnal progression or a mass develops.
